direct_instruction_active_practice.evidence: Each teaching block is followed by a student attempt; however the worked example at turn 40 is dense before asking a check question.

deliberate_practice.evidence: Tutor's arithmetic feedback is repeatedly wrong: at turn 24 says '360-190=170' (correct) but then turn 37 says '360-210=150' (should be 150 — actually 150 is correct, but turn 22 says 80+110=190 then calls 190 'exactly right' after student said 190 — feedback corrupted by tutor arithmetic errors).

mastery_learning.evidence: Tutor moves on at turn 46 declaring 'Now you understand' after a confused exchange about Step 2, without verifying mastery.

cognitive_load.evidence: Turn 13 references a diagram with '8 equal angles' that wasn't shown; turn 40 dumps a 4-step worked example all at once.

layering.evidence: Practice authentically requires addition + subtraction prerequisites (turns 18-24), and the rule is explicitly linked to the 360° concept.

non_interference.evidence: Topic stays on angles-around-a-point; turn 38 briefly introduces straight-line angles, a confusable topic, without discrimination.

interleaving.evidence: Nearly all practice items have the same structure: sum knowns, subtract from 360°; no variation in problem type.

testing_effect.evidence: Tutor does ask retrieval questions (turn 22, 33) rather than revealing answers immediately, though hints become eager at turn 35.

targeted_remediation.evidence: When student fails repeatedly (turns 32, 34), tutor recycles the same problem with pizza analogy rather than diagnosing arithmetic/operation-choice prereq.

strongest_behaviors: Uses scaffolded sub-questions to break down problems (turn 18: 'First, add the two known angles')
Employs concrete analogy (pizza, turn 35) to reframe the add-vs-subtract decision
weakest_behaviors: Tutor commits arithmetic errors and contradicts the student's correct answers (turn 22: student says 190, tutor agrees but earlier turn 20 implied 190 was wrong; turn 31: claims 100+110=210 after student said 200)
Ignores student-generated questions and forces own scripted problems (turns 9, 12, 14, 25, 39 all ignored)

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid tutor arithmetic mutations
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor repeatedly restates the student's number incorrectly, e.g., student says 200, tutor 'confirms' 210, damaging trust and learning.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Before responding, recompute the student's arithmetic yourself. Never restate a number different from what the student wrote without explicitly flagging it as a correction. If the student's arithmetic is wrong, say so explicitly and show the correct value.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates contradictory feedback and prevents the student from being praised for wrong answers.

prompt_recommendations.title: Acknowledge and incorporate student-generated questions
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student offers thoughtful questions (turns 9, 14, 25, 39) that demonstrate engagement, but tutor brushes them aside.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: I see you're thinking about this! But let's focus on the question I just asked you.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When the student poses a math question relevant to the lesson, either solve it together first or briefly acknowledge it and explain you'll return to it — never dismiss without engagement.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Builds rapport; honors student agency; demonstrates the same skill on their example.

prompt_recommendations.title: No phantom diagram references
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor references diagrams that the student cannot see, increasing confusion.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Looking at the diagram, you can see 8 equal angles around a point, each measuring 45°.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Do not reference visual diagrams unless one has actually been rendered in the conversation. Describe angles in words or with simple ASCII if visuals unavailable.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Removes cognitive load from imagined visuals and prevents confusion.

prompt_recommendations.title: Mastery check before advancing
prompt_recommendations.rationale: After a tangled Step 2 exchange, tutor declares understanding without verification.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Perfect! Yes, we used addition in Step 2... Now you understand the complete method.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Before advancing to a new problem type, require the student to correctly solve at least one full problem independently with no arithmetic errors. Do not declare mastery after only confirming a single sub-step.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Gates progression on real evidence, not surface agreement.

prompt_recommendations.title: Vary problem types to enable interleaving
prompt_recommendations.rationale: All practice problems follow the same template (sum-then-subtract), reducing retrieval flexibility.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Three angles around a point are 80°, 110°, and x°. Find x.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: After 2 successful identical-template problems, vary the structure: e.g., give the missing angle and ask the student to find an unknown known; mix in 'is this possible?' or 'how many angles?' questions.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces deeper engagement with the 360° rule rather than rote arithmetic.

prompt_recommendations.title: Diagnose prereq on repeated failure
prompt_recommendations.rationale: After student says 'add more' instead of subtract, tutor just re-frames; no diagnosis of add/subtract concept.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: If the student picks the wrong operation twice, pause the main problem and run a tiny prerequisite check (e.g., 'You have 360 cents, you spent 210. How much is left? What operation did you use?') before resuming.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Targets the actual bottleneck (operation choice) rather than recycling.

flow_recommendations.title: Arithmetic verification middleware
flow_recommendations.rationale: Multiple turns show the tutor confidently asserting wrong sums or subtractions.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Catches numeric mutations server-side before the message reaches the student.

flow_recommendations.title: Suppress duplicate/regenerated turns
flow_recommendations.rationale: Tutor turn 39 appears to echo a previous tutor message back as the student turn — sign of orchestration confusion.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents the conversation from looping or feeding tutor output back as student input.

flow_recommendations.title: Exit-ticket gate per concept
flow_recommendations.rationale: Progression isn't tied to a clean independent solve.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: Now you understand the complete method.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Ensures lesson cannot advance without demonstrated mastery.

experience_recommendations.title: Reduce template fatigue with varied phrasing
experience_recommendations.rationale: Repeated 'Let's try this practice problem' / 'Let's try another' becomes mechanical.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Conversation feels less scripted and more responsive to the student.

experience_recommendations.title: Gentler correction tone after multiple errors
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student is error-prone; repeated 'Not quite' can feel discouraging without specific praise of partial progress.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite — let me clarify Step 2.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Maintains student motivation in the face of multiple misconceptions.

overall_summary: The tutor scaffolds the angles-around-a-point rule with practice problems but suffers from serious arithmetic mutation errors (claiming wrong sums and differences, sometimes contradicting correct student answers), references phantom diagrams, ignores genuine student-generated questions, and declares mastery without verification. Targeted remediation and deliberate-practice quality are the weakest dimensions; layering and active learning are adequate.
